item.title: MCM-Meridian kicks of Week of Wonder with Space Day
item.description: The Mississippi Children’s Museum – Meridian will launch its Week of Wonder during spring break with Space Day on Saturday, March 7, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Guests can blast off into fun with space-themed activities for aspiring astronauts of all ages.

item.title: Our View: Renditions hit local businesses but can be avoided
item.description: While much of the focus this time of year is on homestead exemptions, and rightfully so, it is also time for businesses to turn in their renditions. Under state law, businesses are required to file personal property renditions with the Tax Assessor by April 1.

item.title: CHIN hosts colon cancer awareness Lunch & Learn March 26
item.description: Residents are invited to learn more about their health as the Community Health Improvement Network, the health initiative of The Montgomery Institute, will host a Colon Cancer Awareness Lunch & Learn on Thursday, March 26.

item.title: Thursday law enforcement action yields multiple arrests
item.description: The East Mississippi Drug Task Force on Thursday joined with other law enforcement agencies in a city-wide action resulting in seized drugs and multiple arrests.

item.description: The main character or number one bad girl was Peggy Shippen, known as the Princess of Philadelphia. She is the youngest child of successful Philadelphian, Edwin Shippen, a lawyer and judge.

item.title: Measles today, polio tomorrow?
item.description: Measles hit Spartanburg, South Carolina, hard. Reuters reported last month nearly 1,000 individuals got infected in Spartanburg County since October.

item.title: MCC creatives go big at The MAX
item.description: It’s been a quarter century since guitar master Mitch Brantley began teaching and encouraging students at Meridian Community College, and that collaboration is about to hit a new high mark.
